note: This review found ChatGPT's accuracy varies by subject, strong in economics but weak in maths, and can assist teaching while risking fake information and plagiarism, so schools should update assessments, policies and training now.
title: What Is the Impact of ChatGPT on Education? A Rapid Review of the Literature

reading.body:
ChatGPT's usefulness in education depends on the subject: strong in economics, satisfactory in programming, unsatisfactory in mathematics.

That pattern is the finding. A single model does not deliver one level of quality across a curriculum, so any school or product team treating it as uniformly reliable is making an assumption the reviewed evidence does not support. The same tool that helps an economics student can mislead a maths student, and the review offers no mechanism for predicting which side of that line a new subject falls on.

The review also separates two kinds of use. As an assistant to instructors, generating course materials and suggestions, and as a virtual tutor answering questions and supporting collaboration, ChatGPT has a role. As an assessment tool it creates two problems at once: incorrect or fake information, and students bypassing plagiarism detectors. Those are not the same risk and they do not have the same fix.

The recommended response is institutional rather than technical: update assessment methods, update policies, train instructors, educate students. The data covers 50 articles published between December 2022 and February 2023, a four-month window at the very start of ChatGPT's public life. It says nothing about later models, nothing about cost, and nothing about the compute or power behind any of it.

explain_beginner: A review looked at early research on ChatGPT in education, covering December 2022 to February 2023. It found the chatbot's accuracy depends on the subject. It did very well in economics, was okay at programming, and struggled with mathematics. ChatGPT can help teachers create materials and give students a virtual tutor for questions and group work. But it can also produce false information and let students avoid plagiarism checks. The review says schools and universities should act quickly to change how they assess students, update their rules, and train both teachers and students.
explain_business: This review shows ChatGPT's reliability depends on the subject, strong in economics, weaker in maths, which matters for any organization using it in training or education products. It can support instructors and learners, but it can also generate false information and help users evade plagiarism checks. The practical implication is that schools and universities should not wait. Leaders should update assessment methods and institutional policies now, and invest in training for instructors and students. This informs decisions about adopting AI tools, managing academic integrity risk, and funding staff and student readiness programs.
explain_practitioner: This rapid review analyzed 50 articles from relevant databases and Google Scholar, published December 2022 to February 2023, using open, axial, and selective coding. It examined ChatGPT's capabilities across subjects, educational uses, and researcher-identified issues. Performance ranged from outstanding in economics to satisfactory in programming to unsatisfactory in mathematics. The tool can assist instructors with course materials and suggestions, and act as a virtual tutor answering questions and supporting collaboration. Challenges include incorrect or fake information and bypassing plagiarism detectors. The author recommends immediate updates to assessment methods and institutional policies, plus instructor training and student education.
